Equipment record status

The private inventory documents 20 original photo-derived records plus later fit-out proposals. This index deliberately excludes owner-specific IDs and placement coordinates.

Still open: exact battery SKU and BMS, solar panel, DC panel/fuses, 15 HP motor shaft and transom-bracket rating, 12 L tank connector and ventilation, hose routing, installed positions and physical mass centers.

Open the full 3D viewer, select Inspect stern · motor & tank and inspect the provisional engine, bracket, hose and tank. For an owner handoff, attach the latest exported JSON separately.

Port stern propulsion installation — dimensional reference, not an approved mounting design

Reference engine: 15 HP four-stroke outboard family. Overall example envelope approximately 662 mm long × 336 mm wide × 1,220 mm high (long-shaft reference). Published dry mass ranges 44–49 kg depending on shaft and starting variant; do not use this as an exact installed weight.

Mount: the 3D model now contains a removable external port-transom support bracket and clamp board, with position and construction purely illustrative. It is not verified to support the actual motor. The motor must not be operated without checking the hull/transom rating, mount manufacturer's rating, fasteners, reinforcement and service clearances.

The 1977 Catalina 22 manual recommends a 3–6 HP engine. A 15 HP motor is outside that recommendation; a suitable bracket alone does not establish hull compatibility. Obtain professional structural review and confirm the exact Catalina hull model/year.

Reference tank: compatible 12 L external plastic portable tank, often listed as Suzuki 65000-89L10 (verify connector/variant). Representative dimensions 363 × 265 × 230 mm. It is currently displayed on the cockpit seat solely so the owner can see its scale.

Fuel routing: tank → connector → marine-rated line/primer → engine. The illustrated hose is not an approved run; the tank may need a different compliant storage location. Verify ventilation, vapor isolation from accommodation spaces, drainage, restraint and leak protection, using the actual fuel hose assembly.
